notes.decision: Treated as the chapter number 115 (ⲣ̄=100 + ⲓⲉ̄=15). Appears three times in lines 20-22 around the chapter title in an ornamental triple-marking pattern (opener, mid-title, closer), interrupting the textual flow. Preserved in the Coptic field but rendered as numeric marker '(115)' in English to flag its non-textual function. The recurrence inside line 22 (between ⲙⲁ- and -ⲣⲉ of the negative habitual ⲙⲁⲣⲉ) confirms it is a marginal/decorative element rather than a part of the prose.

The character ⲯ functions consistently for ϣ throughout this kephalaion's title and body (lines 21-33). This is a scribal/orthographic feature distinctive to this section. Translated normally as ϣ-forms: ⲯⲁⲛⲯⲱⲱⲧ = ϣⲁⲛϣⲱⲱⲧ 'when they cut'; ⲯⲱⲛⲉ = ϣⲱⲛⲉ 'be sick/pained'; ⲯⲁⲩⲧⲕⲉⲥ = ϣⲁⲩ-ⲧⲕⲉⲥ 'they habitually pain him' (with ⲧⲕⲉⲥ = ⲧⲕⲁⲥ 'pain, sting' per glossary).

Rendered 'the tip of the head.' ⲡϫⲁⲕ = 'tip, end, peak' (from ϫⲱⲕ 'complete' or ϫⲁⲕ 'edge'); ⲛⲧⲁⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲡⲉ is parsed as a Lycopolitan/scribal form of ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲡⲉ 'of the head' with anomalous ⲛⲧⲁⲛ̄- prefix (possibly a reduplicated genitive marker). Given the context (cutting things on the head and feet without pain), this most plausibly designates the hair on top of the head — what is shaved (ⲯⲱⲃ = ϣⲱⲃ/ϣⲱⲱⲃ?) without causing pain.

Translated as 'the body.' The form ⲡⲉⲱⲙⲁ is anomalous; standard Coptic is ⲡⲥⲱⲙⲁ (Greek σῶμα). Most likely either (a) a scribal slip omitting the ⲥ-, or (b) a Lycopolitan dialectal variant ⲡⲉ-ⲱⲙⲁ where ⲱⲙⲁ reflects a reduced form. The reading 'body' is required by the parallel ⲡⲥⲱⲙⲁ ⲧⲛⲧⲁⲛⲧ ⲁⲡⲕⲁⲍ 'the body is likened to the land' in line 7, which is the explicit topic of the kephalaion.

The verb is a causative on ⲟⲩⲱⲛϩ̄/ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲥ 'manifest, raise up to view' (per accumulated vocabulary entry ⲁⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲉ 'make known/reveal'). Translated 'make known forth.' This is the standard disciple-petition verb in the Kephalaia for requesting an apostolic exposition.

notes.decision: The framing direct correspondence: 'the body IS likened to the land' (using ⲧⲛⲧⲁⲛⲧ qualitative — cf. accumulated entry). The members within it correspondingly IS likened to ⲛ̄ⲱⲏⲛ 'trees' (Lyc ⲡⲱⲏⲛ = ⲡϣⲏⲛ, in glossary). The kephalaion thus opens with a layered correspondential identification — body:land :: members:trees — preparing the parable that follows about which trees regrow when cut.

Parsed as ⲉ-ϣⲁ-ⲕ-ⲟⲛⲧⲟⲩ 'when one (habitually) plants/sets them' — agricultural verb in line with the tree-planting context. The ⲟⲛⲧ⸗ stem may reflect ⲡⲱⲛⲧ̄/ⲱⲛⲧ̄ 'set, place' (cf. tentative glossary entry ⲱⲛⲧⲟⲩ 'match/correspond them' but here in concrete agricultural register). Translated 'plants them' as the contextually required action; the verb governs the trees' subsequent sprouting and standing fast.

ⲱⲁⲧⲟⲩ from ϣⲱⲱⲧ 'cut, cut down' (in accumulated vocab as ϣⲱϩⲧ 'cutting'); ⲙⲁⲩⲣⲱⲧ negative habitual 'they do not grow.' The antithetical pair structures the parable: trees that regrow when cut versus trees that do not. This botanical taxonomy underlies the moral-anthropological teaching about which embodied desires can be eradicated and which persist.

Greek ἀκαθαρσία 'impurity, uncleanness' (Lyc plural ⲁⲕⲁⲫⲁⲣⲥⲓⲁ with ⲫ for θ — regular Lyc orthography). ⲛⲧⲟⲩⲁⲙ likely Lyc for 'of their food/eating' (ⲟⲩⲱⲙ 'eat'). The phrase 'in the impurities of their food/eating' fits the kephalaion's bodily-discipline register: the trees that regrow when cut are nourished by impure food, an image for the regrowing desires sustained by the unclean nourishment of the flesh.

Translated 'this flesh which is desire-arousing forth.' ⲗⲉϩⲗⲁϩⲧ is the qualitative of the desire-arousing root (per accumulated vocab entry ⲗⲉϩⲗⲁϩⲧ 'desire-arousing/lust-inciting'). The lust-inciting flesh is the ground of the regrowing-tree members of the body — the very desires that, when 'cut,' grow back from their impure root. Closes the kephalaion's botanical parable with the explicit naming of the corresponding moral-physical reality.

Lexeme uncertain. Possible analyses: (a) ⲙⲁⲛ-ⲥⲁⲧⲡ̄ 'place of choice/election' (compound on ⲙⲁⲛ- 'place of' + ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'choose'), with Lyc. ⲍ for ⲛ — fits Manichaean cosmological vocabulary; (b) corrupt scribal form. Preserved untranslated pending parallels.

Lexeme uncertain. Most plausibly ⲁϯ-ϩⲟⲩⲏⲛⲓⲁ, where -ϩⲟⲩⲏⲛⲓⲁ may render Greek εὔνοια 'goodwill, attentive disposition' (with Lyc. ⲍ-onset and vowel adjustment), giving 'with attention/goodwill.' The construction with ⲥⲱⲧⲙ̄ ('hear') + adverbial complement supports an attentive-listening sense. Preserved untranslated pending parallel attestations.
ⲁϩⲍⲙⲉⲥⲧ = ⲁϥ-ϩⲙⲟⲟⲥ-(ⲧ) Lyc. perfect 3sg.m of ϩⲙⲟⲟⲥ 'sit' (with ⲍ for ϩ regular Lyc.) + ⲁⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ 'downward' (in glossary). Standard Coptic 'he sat down' — closes the previous chapter's narrative frame.
